title: Tablet I: "He who saw the Deep"
summary: Introduction to Gilgamesh, king of Uruk. Creation of Enkidu. The wild man and the trapper.

witnesses.note: Also contains Tablet XI (Flood). Principal MS for both.
witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, upper right corner, 2 columns of inscription on either side, 49 and 51 lines + 45 and 49 lines. Neo-Assyrian. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 11, story of the Flood.
Fragment of a clay tablet, 9 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian.Left-hand corner. Fragment of a mythological legend belonging to a tablet of the series. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 8.

title: Tablet II: Enkidu comes to Uruk
summary: Enkidu is civilized. He challenges Gilgamesh. They become friends.

witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 24 + 24 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian. Upper portion, right half. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 7.

title: Tablet III: The elders' counsel
summary: The elders advise Gilgamesh. Ninsun prays to Shamash. Preparation for the Cedar Forest.

witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 21 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian.Lower portion, left half. Probably a continuation of K. 3252. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 4.

title: Tablet IV: Journey to the Cedar Forest
summary: Five dream sequences on the journey. Gilgamesh and Enkidu approach Humbaba.

witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 20 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian.

title: Tablet V: Battle with Humbaba
summary: They enter the Cedar Forest. Defeat of Humbaba with Shamash's help.

witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 22 + 18 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian. Upper portion, left half. Colophon. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 10.

title: Tablet VI: Ishtar's proposal
summary: Ishtar proposes to Gilgamesh. He refuses. The Bull of Heaven.

witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 18 + 24 + 17 + 21 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 10.

title: Tablet VII: Death of Enkidu
summary: The gods decree Enkidu must die. His deathbed vision of the underworld.

witnesses.note: Continuation from Tablet VI on same physical tablet
witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 18 + 24 + 17 + 21 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 10.

title: Tablet VIII: Gilgamesh mourns Enkidu
summary: Lament for Enkidu. Gilgamesh commissions a statue. The funeral.

summary: The tavern-keeper Siduri. The ferryman Urshanabi. Crossing the Waters of Death.

witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, 15 + 13 lines of inscription. Neo-Assyrian.Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 12.

title: Tablet XI: The Flood
summary: Utnapishtim tells the Flood story. The plant of youth. Return to Uruk.

witnesses.note: The famous "Flood Tablet" — most complete single tablet of the epic
witnesses.description: Fragment of a clay tablet, upper right corner, 2 columns of inscription on either side, 49 and 51 lines + 45 and 49 lines. Neo-Assyrian. Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet 11, story of the Flood.

title: Tablet XII: Enkidu and the Netherworld
summary: Appendix. Enkidu's spirit describes the underworld. (Later addition, translated from Sumerian.)

witnesses.atf:
@obverse
1. EN GAL-u₂ LUGAL DINGIR-MEŠ {d}NIN.URTA iš-pu-ra-an-ni
#tr.de: Der große Herr, der König der Götter, Ninurta, hat mich gesandt.
2. a-na ru-be₂-e ti-ri-iṣ qa-ti-ia
#tr.de: Dem Fürsten, meinem verlängerten Arm,
3. a-na ma-hir {giš}haṭ-ṭi {giš}GU.ZA u₃ BALA-e
#tr.de: dem, der Szepter, Thron und Amt empfing,
4. a-na GIR₃.NITA₂ ša qa-ti-ia °\° qi₂-bi-ma
#tr.de: dem Statthalter meiner Gnaden sprich,
5. um-ma {d}NIN.URTA EN GAL-u₂ DUMU {d}en-lil₂ [ša]r-ru-um-ma
#tr.de: Dies (verkündet dir) Ninurta, der große Herr, der Sohn Enlils, der König:
6. uš-šu-ša₂-ku ra-aʾ-ba-ku ze-na-ku [(u₃) š]ab-sa-ku
#tr.de: Ich war sehr erzürnt, rasend, zornig (und) wütend.
7. uš-šu-ša₂-ku man-nu li-[ni-i]h-ha-an-ni
#tr.de: Wenn ich erzürnt bin, wer vermag mich da zu beruhigen?
8. ra-aʾ-ba-ku man-nu li#-sal#-lim-an-ni
#tr.de: Wenn ich rasend bin, wer vermag mich da zu beschwichtigen?
9. ze-na-ku a-na E₂-ia man-nu li-še-ri-ba-an-ni
#tr.de: Wenn ich gegenüber meinem Haus in Zorn verfallen bin, wer bringt mich in es zurück?
10. a-bar-ša₂ a-na ba-ni-šu [b]a-ni {d}AMAR.UTU
#tr.de: Wahrlich, seinem Erbauer, dem Erbauer Marduk
11. a-a-in-na ta-mi-tu# [(x) x]-u₂ ki-lal-lu-ni
#tr.de: Wo Eid/Wortlaut ... uns beide?
12. ta-rib ni-du-ku-m[a (x x x)] x-bad# dan niš-tu-u₂
#tr.de: Der Ersatz? (für die?), die? wir töteten un[d deren? ..]. @i{wir tranken}
13. u₃ ina MUD₂-ša₂ u₂#/e#/kal#/ga# [x x x] x qa-ti-ni
#tr.de: und mit deren Blut wir?] unsere Hände [@i{besudelten}]
14. at-ta ki-i i[a?-a?-ti? x] aq-bak-ka#
#tr.de: Du bist wie @i{i}[@i{ch} (...)] sagte ich zu dir.
15. a-na DUMU [...] x en [x]
#tr.de: Dem Sohn ...
16. a-na D[UMU?.MUNUS? ...] pa [x]
#tr.de: Der @i{T}[@i{ochter} ...]
17. ša₂ i#-[...] x da# [x (x)]
